Make the next connection easier.

Quick readMore contextTechnical detailSpeaker notes

A useful idea can stall before it reaches a suitable program, institution, or partner. These proposals focus on the handoff: who can help, who takes responsibility, and whether the connection actually happens.

A pilot to discuss: supported referrals

Identify a receiving partner and a navigator. Begin with a small set of independent researchers or community-led questions.

Progress: Measure completed handoffs and time to useful support.

Why this belongs on the agenda

The resource guide asks who faces barriers because of networks, location, institutional size, or access to infrastructure. Community relationships also belong in the innovation ecosystem.

Define the pilot before judging it

Agree on the intended user, the barrier, a named owner, the starting conditions, and the evidence needed to judge progress. Preserve limitations and reasons for changing direction. A proposed pilot is not a funded program or a completed evaluation.

Convening prompt: three changes over the next five years, p. 15. Select a topic above for the specific example, proposal, and evidence.

Participant proposals for the Widener-led, NSF-funded convening. Project examples include documented results, work in development, and proposed pilots.
